As I contemplated the completed grid, "banana boat" caught my attention. I realized us Poles don't call that inflatable banana you can ride on the water an actual boat - it's simply a banana, to us. I googled "banana boat" out of curiosity, anyway, and learned that not only is it a name for a novelty seaside ride - it was also a type of fast cargo ship used to transport bananas from the tropics before modern technology allowed them to keep for longer.

Also, generally speaking, our "łódź" has a narrower meaning than your "boat" - in English "a boat" may be a synonym of "a ship", but in Polish łódź is a small vessel by definition, so a ship (statek) would never be called a łódź.

Our cultures may be different but "Break a leg!" functions as an expression in Polish, too. We say "Połamania nóg!" which translates into "May you break your legs!" (Noga is the nominative case of a singular leg, nogi are plural legs in the nominative, and nóg is the genitive case of nogi; nogi is also the genitive of a singular noga - I can only imagine what horror learning Polish must be to an English speaker 🤣).

Note on 68A:
The great writer of speculative fiction, Stanislaw Lem (Hi, Andrzej!), has a short story--one of his "fables for robots"--titled "the Three Electroknights":
There exists, in the remotest regions of the Cosmos, the planet Cryonia, whose surface temperature is just a degree or two above Zero Kelvin--cold enough that elemental gases--hydrogen, argon, krypton--exist as crystalline solids, from which the Cryonids fashion gemstones of legendary beauty. Cryonia is raided, successively, by the titular electroknights, who attempt to steal the jewels; but in each case their heat causes the stones to vaporize.

A metaphor for vanity and avarice.

A single is a subset of hits.  If the runner ends up on second or third base, it's a two base or a three base hit, aka a double or a triple.

A home run is also a hit, but rarely called that because it's a special kind of hit that leaves no runners on base.

The batter is also credited with a hit with a sacrifice play, where even though the batter is out, the runners advance on the bases.  The most common example of that is a sacrifice bunt which moves a runner from first to second.
